title: Review: Describing motion; Motion graphs; Constant-acceleration equations; Projectile motion; Forces and free-body diagrams; Newton's first law and equilibrium; Newton's second law; Drag and terminal velocity; Moments and static equilibrium; Systems and centre of mass
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: D11-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; K03-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; K02-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; K02-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: D01-1#N.12, D02-1#N.9, D08-1#N.7, D01-1#N.14, D02-1#N.11, D01-1#N.9, D02-1#N.4, D03-1#N.7a, D07-1#N.5, D08-1#N.5a, D11-1#N.3, K01-1#N.10. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Fluid
items.clue: Any liquid or gas through which an object moves.

items.label: Free fall
items.clue: Motion in which gravity is the only force acting on the object.

items.label: Acceleration
items.clue: Gradient of a velocity–time graph; uniform when the line is straight.

items.label: Distance
items.clue: Whole area on a velocity–time graph with every part counted as positive.

questions.stem: A crate is given a push and then slides down a rough ramp on its own. Which list gives all the forces acting on the crate while it slides, and no others?

options.text: Weight, normal force, friction up the ramp and a force of motion down the ramp
Weight, normal force and friction down the ramp
Weight, normal force from the ramp and friction up the ramp
Weight, a separate force down the slope, normal force and friction

questions.explanation: Earth pulls down; the ramp pushes perpendicular to its surface and, as the crate slides down it, rubs back up it. Three forces, each with a source.

questions.stem: Three forces act at a point. Which set of magnitudes could keep the point in equilibrium?

options.text: 2 N, 3 N and 6 N
5 N, 7 N and 11 N
4 N, 4 N and 9 N
3 N, 5 N and 9 N

questions.explanation: 11 N is less than 5 N + 7 N = 12 N, so the three can form a closed triangle at suitable angles. Their resultant can be zero.

questions.stem: A tap handle is turned by two equal and opposite forces of 12 N, applied at the two ends of a handle 0.050 m long, each perpendicular to the handle. What is the turning effect of this couple?

options.text: 1.2 N m
0 N m

questions.explanation: One force × perpendicular distance between the lines of action: 12 × 0.050 = 0.60 N m.

questions.stem: A hockey puck is hit by a stick and then slides across level ice. Friction and air resistance are negligible. Which forces are exerted on the puck while it slides, after it has left the stick?

options.text: Earth's pull, the ice's push and a fading push left over from the hit
A downward pull by Earth and an upward push by the ice that touches it
A downward pull by Earth, and no force at all from the ice
An upward push by the ice, with no gravitational force on a supported puck

questions.stem: Which of the following objects is in translational equilibrium?

options.text: A ball at the top of its flight, momentarily at rest
A car rounding a curve on a level road at a constant speed
A puck slowing down on rough ice after a stick stops pushing it
A crate riding up a straight conveyor at a steady 2 m s⁻¹

questions.explanation: Its speed and direction are both constant, so its velocity is constant and the net force on it is zero: friction from the belt, up the slope, balances the component of its weight down the slope, and the normal force balances the rest.

questions.stem: A ball has been thrown straight up and is still rising. Air resistance is not negligible; the upthrust of the air is negligible. Which list gives all the forces acting on the ball, and no others?

options.text: Weight downwards and an upward force from the throw
Weight downwards and drag upwards
Weight and drag, both downwards
Weight only

questions.explanation: Earth pulls down; drag opposes the velocity, which is upwards, so drag also points down. Both slow the ball.

questions.stem: A puck slides east at constant velocity across level ice with negligible friction. Starting at time t, a constant force directed north is exerted on the puck, and no other horizontal force acts. Which statement describes the puck's motion after time t?

options.text: It turns and moves due north, in the direction of the force on it.
Its eastward velocity decreases while its northward velocity increases.
It moves at a constant velocity in a direction between east and north.
Its eastward velocity stays the same while its northward velocity increases.

questions.stem: Block X (2.0 kg) and block Y (4.0 kg) rest on a frictionless horizontal surface, joined by a light string. A horizontal force of 24 N pulls X away from Y, and both accelerate together. What is the tension in the string?
questions.explanation: System: a = 24 ÷ 6.0 = 4.0 m s⁻². Y alone: the only horizontal force is the tension, T = 4.0 × 4.0 = 16 N.

questions.stem: A rectangular wooden sign hangs from a single hook through a hole at the middle of its top edge. A heavy metal letter is fixed near the sign's left end. How does the sign hang at rest?

options.text: Level, because the hook is at the middle of the top edge.
Tilted, left end lower, with its centre of gravity directly below the hook.
Tilted, left end lower, until the metal letter is directly below the hook.
Tilted, right end lower, to balance the heavy letter.

questions.explanation: At rest the weight has no moment about the hook, so its line of action passes through the hook. The sign turns until its centre of gravity, shifted left by the letter, is vertically below the hook.

questions.stem: A uniform beam of length 5.0 m and weight 400 N rests horizontally on two supports, one at each end, P and Q. A person of weight 600 N stands on the beam 1.0 m from Q. What is the upward force from support P?
questions.explanation: Taking moments about Q: F_P × 5.0 = 400 × 2.5 + 600 × 1.0 = 1600 N m, so F_P = 320 N.

questions.stem: A small steel ball is released from rest in air and falls until it reaches terminal velocity. How does its acceleration change during this time?

options.text: It is constant but less than g, because drag is constant.
It stays equal to g, since drag only lowers the ball's speed.
It increases, since the ball moves faster and faster as it falls.
It decreases from g towards zero as the drag increases.

questions.explanation: At release the ball is at rest, so there is no drag and its acceleration is g. As it speeds up the drag grows, so the acceleration decreases, reaching zero at terminal velocity.

questions.stem: A car travels 3.0 km along a straight road at a constant speed of 10 m s⁻¹, then returns along the same road to its starting point at a constant speed of 15 m s⁻¹. What are its average speed and its average velocity for the whole journey?

options.text: Average speed 12.5 m s⁻¹; average velocity 0 m s⁻¹
Average speed 12 m s⁻¹; average velocity 0 m s⁻¹
Average speed 12 m s⁻¹; average velocity 12 m s⁻¹
Average speed 12 m s⁻¹; average velocity −2.5 m s⁻¹
